title: Bone Folio — Drift-Style Serif Opener
description: A type-only opener in the lineage of The Drift and n+1: a long titular phrase in transitional serif anchored asymmetrically to the upper-left, paired with a hairline Roman numeral in the opposing corner. No imagery, no colour blocks — the page is the entire argument.
philosophy: This template trusts language above all else and refuses to dress it in anything that would compete. It exists for the speaker who believes a room should quiet down before the first word is spoken — not be seduced by motion graphics or stock photography. Asymmetric weight and deliberate negative space create tension without spectacle. It is for essayists, literary critics, and humanist academics who value the gravity of a well-chosen sentence over the velocity of a designed moment.
goodFor: Literary magazine and journal article opener slides
Author readings and essay-based talk title cards
Humanities conference keynote openers with no supporting imagery
Single-author long-form essay or lecture introductions
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly reviews or data-dense financial reports
Product launches requiring photography, illustration, or brand visuals
Fast-paced sales pitches demanding high colour energy and motion
Multi-column content slides with dense bullet-point body copy
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like the opening page of a literary journal — The Drift or n+1 — where the act of reading is itself the drama. Typographic mass sits in asymmetric tension with vast, unhurried negative space, as if the title has been set deliberately beside a silence rather than above it. The mood is austere and patient, carrying the gravity of a well-chosen sentence before an audience has settled into their chairs. Avoid illustrative imagery, colour fills, geometric ornamentation, or any element that would compete with the authority of language.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with an outer margin of roughly 8%; the title phrase is anchored flush to the upper-left, occupying columns 1–8 and dropping to approximately 20% from the top of the slide — a weighted descent rather than a centred float. A hairline Roman numeral sits pinned to the lower-right, baseline-aligned to the bottom margin, acting as a distant counterweight. No header band, no footer bar, no decorative rules; everything outside the two type elements is unbroken negative space. Hierarchy is established through extreme scale contrast between the title mass and the numeral alone.

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like a journal page encountered mid-essay — unhurried, confident, trusting language alone to hold attention. A single extended quote or thesis statement anchors left-center with asymmetric weight, while attribution or a marginal gloss drifts to the far right, generating quiet horizontal tension. The compositional rhythm is slow and deliberate: one dominant text moment, one understated counterpoint, and abundant surrounding stillness that gives both room to matter. Avoid any imagery, tonal fills, or decorative marks beyond a single hairline accent rule.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid; the primary text block — a pull quote or compressed thesis — occupies columns 2–8, leaving a wide right margin for a floating attribution line or marginal gloss in a smaller weight. A single hairline rule divides the main text moment from its credit beneath it, positioned at roughly mid-page height. Roman numeral or folio number anchors bottom-right, outside the text column. No header band; the upper quarter of the slide is preserved as open negative space, and outer margins bleed with at least 8% breathing room.
